reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the course promotes a BitConnect referral and account-funding pathway requiring at least $100 and instructs viewers to exchange Bitcoin for BitConnect. It encourages lending by claiming returns of up to 0.25% daily and a first interest payment the next day, framing the activity as a way to act quickly and profit. The records do not establish that anyone transferred funds, received returns, or experienced a loss, and they do not independently verify the external service.

opening.argument: Judge the lending instructions in full: before the participant confirms, the walkthrough presents a terms-and-conditions acknowledgment stating that participation is a decision made with an understanding of the rules and regulations. It also tells the participant to review the loan details before confirming. Those steps support reading this as an explanation of a financial process in which the participant must make a choice, not a claim that the presenter can make that choice risk-free for them.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited daily percentage is phrased as what a participant is "capable of earning," not as evidence that anyone actually received that rate. The example amount is likewise introduced as a hypothetical entry. The account-funding and wallet-payment steps show what the walkthrough tells viewers to do; they do not establish that a viewer completed a loan. The prosecution also leaves out the required acknowledgment of terms before confirmation.

Please verify terms and conditions I read the terms of use and I make decision to participate the BitConnect system with full understanding of rules and regulations.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging terms is not a substantive risk warning. The walkthrough directs viewers to make a loan and claims they can earn daily profits through a trading bot; it then says they will receive an interest payment the next day. No completed viewer transaction is needed to recognize that the video promotes and instructs participation in this return-seeking lending scheme.

opening.argument: This is organized as a course, beginning with an explanation of Bitcoin and blockchain and then teaching what a cryptocurrency wallet is and how to use one. Even the later account section is presented as a numbered walkthrough of dashboard controls and exchange steps. A careful reading should distinguish a tutorial describing an interface from proof that the presenter handled anyone's money or that a viewer made a transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's funding quote appears in a lesson that walks through dashboard steps. Its payment-button quote identifies a control in that walkthrough, not an observed payment. The percentage quote reports what the lesson says a participant could earn; it is not independent verification of a return. Those distinctions matter when assessing what the video itself establishes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The lesson format does not neutralize its instructions. It tells viewers to fund a BitConnect account, buy BitConnect Coin, make a loan and start earning. The course explicitly connects that loan to daily profits from a purported trading bot. The issue is what the video promotes, not whether the record proves a viewer followed through.

opening.argument: The description openly identifies a BitConnect referral link, while the walkthrough describes a participant using their own wallet to choose an amount and place an exchange order. It even describes selecting from people currently selling the coin. The record therefore shows a disclosed referral and described marketplace activity; it does not show a viewer using the link, surrendering credentials to the presenter, or receiving a return. That narrower evidentiary reading should govern the decision.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a funding minimum, a hypothetical loan amount and a wallet-payment button, but those are instructions and interface details, not evidence of a completed deposit or paid interest. The lending quote describes a claimed way to earn; it does not independently establish the bot's operation or any viewer's outcome. The disclosed referral and exchange context should not be collapsed into proof of a completed scam.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Disclosure of a referral does not make the promoted activity ordinary commerce. The video instructs viewers to convert Bitcoin into BitConnect Coin, then directs them to make a loan and claims daily interest through a proprietary trading bot. A completed deposit, credential request or independently verified payout is not necessary to identify that promotional mechanism.
